title: Languages recognized within a tree-size bound
statement: For a function $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, a language $L$ of Boolean words has tree size bounded by $T$ if there is a family of Boolean tree circuits $(C_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, with $C_n$ acting on $n$ variables, such that $\mathrm{size}(C_n)\le T(n)$ for every $n$, and every Boolean word $w$ belongs to $L$ exactly when $C_{|w|}$ evaluates to true on the coordinates of $w$.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ is a function from natural numbers to natural numbers
$L$ is a language of Boolean words
For each natural number $n$, a tree circuit $C_n$ on $n$ variables exists
For every Boolean word $w$, membership in $L$ is equivalent to $C_{|w|}$ evaluating to true on $w$
